_comment: Exercise demonstration clips. Each clip has a SETUP POSTURE (supine/prone/side-lying/quadruped/seated/half-kneeling) plus joint-angle keyframes at real physiological range.
_v5_fix: v4 authored every clip standing at ~45% of range. A glute bridge is done lying on your back, so a standing bridge just swayed the legs; and 15 degrees of hip flexion is not a Romanian deadlift. Postures + full range fix both.
_axes: Degrees, Euler XYZ on the named pose bone. Posture is applied as a static offset on every keyframe so a clip is self-contained.
_mirror: Authored on the LEFT; the viewer mirrors for the right side.

squat.label: Squat
squat.notes: Closed-chain like the hinge: hips and knees fold while the feet stay flat.

hinge.label: Hip hinge / Romanian deadlift
hinge.notes: 60 degrees of hip flexion, which is what lengthens the hamstrings (they run pelvis->tibia). The rig is pelvis-rooted, so the body pivots about the hips rather than keeping the heels planted -- holding a ground contact through this range needs a real IK solve, not a joint-angle clip. Counter-rotating Hips to fake it does not work: Hips is the rig root and carries the spine, arms and head with it, which visibly tore the body apart.

bridge.label: Glute bridge
bridge.notes: Supine. The pelvis rises through hip extension while the shoulders and feet stay down; on a pelvis-rooted rig that is a Hips rotation plus femur swing. An earlier revision dropped the Hips track and left only 20 degrees of femur motion -- which reproduced the original 'just sways the legs' complaint via a fix for something else.

hip_thrust.label: Hip thrust
hip_thrust.notes: Supine. The pelvis rises through hip extension while the shoulders and feet stay down; on a pelvis-rooted rig that is a Hips rotation plus femur swing. An earlier revision dropped the Hips track and left only 20 degrees of femur motion -- which reproduced the original 'just sways the legs' complaint via a fix for something else.

hip_abduction.label: Side-lying hip abduction
hip_abduction.notes: Side-lying: with the pelvis rolled 90 degrees the abduction axis becomes x, not z. Measured 61cm of foot travel on x versus 10cm on y.

leg_raise.label: Supine straight-leg raise
leg_raise.notes: Supine hamstring stretch: hip flexes to 80 with the knee locked straight.

nordic.label: Nordic hamstring curl (eccentric)
nordic.notes: Kneeling, body lowers forward as the knees extend under eccentric hamstring load.

dead_bug.label: Dead bug
dead_bug.notes: Supine, opposite arm and leg extend away from a braced trunk.

measured_from.match: same supine hip-flexion pattern, one limb at a time

quad_setting.label: Quadriceps setting
quad_setting.notes: Long-sitting knee extension: the terminal-range contraction that activates VMO.

spine_flexion.label: Cat-cow
spine_flexion.notes: Quadruped, not standing. Segmental flexion summed along 14 vertebral bones reaches real cat-cow range.

spine_extension.label: Thoracic extension
spine_extension.notes: Supine over a roller, extending the thoracic spine.

hip_flexor_stretch.label: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
hip_flexor_stretch.notes: Half-kneeling setup, then the rear hip drives into extension -- that IS the stretch.

shoulder_abduction.label: Shoulder abduction
shoulder_abduction.notes: Full 160 with scapular upward rotation -- shoulder abduction is never purely glenohumeral.

shoulder_rotation.label: Shoulder external rotation
shoulder_rotation.notes: Elbow held at 90 (the setup) while the humerus rotates externally through 70.

row.label: Row / face pull
row.notes: Starts with the arm reached forward and pulls back -- v4 authored it from a dead-hang, so nothing read as a row.

prone_y_raise.label: Prone Y raise
prone_y_raise.notes: Prone, arms lifting off the floor into a Y.

serratus_punch.label: Supine serratus punch
serratus_punch.notes: Supine with the arm vertical; the movement is scapular protraction, not arm motion.

elbow_extension.label: Overhead triceps extension
elbow_extension.notes: Arm stays overhead (the setup); the elbow extends from 130 to nearly straight.

forearm_rotation.label: Supination / pronation
forearm_rotation.notes: Pronation/supination is LeftForeArm.z on this rig, not .y (measured: y moves the hand 2.4cm, z moves it 36cm). Radius.l is DAMPED_TRACK-driven by LeftForeArm, so keyframing the radius directly does nothing at all.

nerve_glide.label: Median nerve glide
nerve_glide.notes: Nerve glides deliberately combine one lengthening end with one slackening end.

grip.label: Grip / release
grip.notes: Full fist closure across every phalanx.

finger_extension.label: Finger extension
finger_extension.notes: Starts from a closed fist and opens -- the reverse of grip.

neck_flexion.label: Chin tuck
neck_flexion.notes: Chin tuck: upper cervical (Head) flexes while the lower segments stay long. Driven through Neck-Start/Neck1/Head -- keyframing C1..C7 directly does nothing, they are ARMATURE-constraint children of these.

jaw_open.label: Jaw opening
jaw_open.notes: 30 degrees of mandibular depression -- roughly 40mm interincisal, a normal full opening.

breathing.label: Diaphragmatic breathing
breathing.notes: Rib expansion is genuinely a few degrees -- flagged small_range so the range-of-motion test cannot be satisfied by a weak angle here.

ankle_eversion.label: Ankle eversion
ankle_eversion.notes: Peroneals evert the foot; distinct from dorsiflexion, which is why banded eversion needed its own clip.

leg_press.label: 45° Incline Leg Press
leg_press.notes: Closed-chain 45-degree incline leg press with diamond-plate carriage contact.

_unused_note: lunge, clamshell, shoulder_flexion, neck_rotation and neck_extension are movement patterns the library exposes for browsing by muscle even where no single exercise is currently mapped to them.
_relative: Track angles are RELATIVE to the clip's posture, which is applied as a base offset. Writing absolute angles in a posed clip double-counts the posture (a supine bridge with Hips.x=-90 on top of the -90 supine posture came out standing again).
_vertebrae: L1..L5/T1..T12/C1..C7 are ARMATURE-constraint children of LowerBack/Spine/Spine1 and Neck-Start/Neck1/Head. Keyframes on them are silently overridden (measured 0.6cm of travel vs 33cm through the control bones), so all spine and neck clips drive the control bones.
_driven_bones: Ulna/Radius (DAMPED_TRACK from LeftForeArm), Clavicle-X/Z (LOCKED_TRACK from Shoulder) and the individual vertebrae/phalanges are all constraint-driven. Keyframing them is silently discarded. Only the control bones are keyframable.
_posture_impl: A posture is a rotation of the ARMATURE OBJECT plus, where the limbs differ from standing, a few static bone angles. It is NOT a rotation of the Hips bone. Rotating Hips looked right in isolation but propagates through the rig UNEVENLY -- the arms hang off T1, which is a separate root bone following the torso via an ARMATURE constraint, so at -90 the head travelled 100cm while the arm travelled 23cm and the body visibly stretched apart. Rotating the object moves every bone rigidly, which is what 'lying down' actually means.
_arms: The Z-Biomechanics rest pose holds the arms in anatomical position (abducted). Bringing them to the side needs the shoulder's real adduction axis plus scapular counter-motion; a naive LeftArm.z offset in the posture wrecked the whole pose. Left as the rig's own rest pose for now -- arm clips read correctly against it, they just start from arms-out rather than arms-at-side. Recorded as a known limit rather than shipped broken.
_postures_solved: Postures are SOLVED, not guessed: a search over hip/knee/shoulder angles minimising 'the parts that touch the floor end up at the same height, with the hips above them'. The hand-written half-kneeling pose put the rear FOOT at head height (measured y=+0.77 vs head y=+0.74), which is what made the legs render as ribbons flying off the body. Guessing joint angles for a multi-joint posture does not work; solving for the contact constraint does.
_seated: Only quad_setting stays seated -- long-sitting terminal knee extension IS the exercise. The arm and hand clips were seated for realism, but two straight legs across the frame made the camera fit the LEGS and shrink the arm you are meant to watch.
_provenance: Clips are MEASURED from CC-licensed human exercise video via MediaPipe pose estimation (see tools/mocap.py), SHAPED (clinical amplitude + measured human timing curve) where single-camera video cannot resolve the movement, or STATIC. Each clip carries a `source` field. Video credits in ATTRIBUTION.md.
